properties_verified.test_file: tests/test_lightning_indexer.py + tests/test_dsa_topk_selection.py (same reference functions compose to model the fused kernel's score-then-topk behavior)
checks: covered transitively: indexer_score/indexer_scores_for_query (Eq.1) feeding into topk_select/indexer_then_sparse_attention (Eq.2) is exactly the score->ReLU->weighted-sum->top-k pipeline the fused NPU kernel implements; no separate test file needed since dossier marks this mechanism 'supporting' with no unique numerical claim beyond composing the two already-tested primitives
aggregate_main_attention L1-normalizes the per-head sum to a valid distribution (Eq.3's p_{t,:})
dense_warmup_kl is ~0 (< 1e-6) when indexer logits are a monotone transform of p (perfect alignment) -- Eq.3 identity boundary
dense_warmup_kl is large (> 0.5) for a deliberately misaligned indexer -- confirms the loss is sensitive, not degenerate
sparse_stage_kl restricted to a selected subset is ~0 when that subset is internally aligned (Eq.4 boundary)

topk_mass_recall is maximal and exactly equal to the true top-k probability mass when indexer ranking matches p exactly; strictly worse for a ranking that inverts true importance (both deterministic, no randomness)
alpha=0 in simulate_indexer_logits recovers the exact same top-k ranking as the true distribution (monotone transform sanity check, seed=9)

flagship statistical test: sweeping the alignment knob alpha in {0.0,0.3,0.6,1.0} with 50 trials per level (seed = 1000*trial + 10*alpha for full reproducibility), average KL strictly increases end-to-end (alpha=0 is the global min) and average top-k mass recall strictly decreases end-to-end (alpha=0 is the global max) -- this is the quantitative form of paper's central co-adaptation claim that low indexer/true-attention KL is what makes top-k pruning not lose retrieval mass. Uses monotonic endpoint comparison (avg_kl[0]<avg_kl[-1] and == min; avg_recall[0]>avg_recall[-1] and == max) rather than requiring every adjacent midpoint to be monotonic, specifically to avoid flakiness from sampling noise at n_trials=50.
decode_step_main_cost_dense/sparse and decode_step_indexer_cost match the O(L*d), O(k*d), O(L*H^I*d^I) closed forms exactly on hand-picked numbers (deterministic)
main_only_speedup at L=131072,k=512 equals exactly context_len/k == 256.0 (matches dossier's worked-example '~256x' claim, per_kv_dim algebraically cancels out of the ratio)
main_only_speedup at k=2048 (paper's training value) equals exactly 64.0 (matches dossier's '~64x' claim)

end_to_end_speedup (including indexer cost) is strictly less than main_only_speedup but still > 1.0 -- confirms the report never overstates the win by ignoring indexer cost, and that indexer cost does not erase the net gain
vllm_ascend_deployment_numbers() (k=512 default) and paper_training_numbers() (k=2048) reproduce the same 256x/64x figures via the named convenience wrappers
paper's k=2048 yields strictly smaller speedup than deployment's k=512 for both main-only and end-to-end figures (more tokens selected -> less speedup, as expected)

notes: All 9 dossier mechanisms have direct test coverage (lightning-indexer-fused-kernel covered transitively via the two primitive test files it composes, per dossier's own 'supporting, no unique numerical claim' classification). No training loop / gradient descent was implemented or tested, matching impl-notes.md's explicit scope boundary (Eq.3/4 are used only as loss *definitions* to measure alignment-quality tradeoffs, not as an optimizer to run -- paper does not publish enough hyperparameter detail to responsibly reconstruct the actual training loop). Flagship statistical test (test_lower_kl_correlates_with_higher_topk_mass_recall_across_alignment_sweep) uses fixed per-trial seeds and an endpoint-monotonicity assertion (not per-adjacent-step monotonicity) specifically to keep the check robust against sampling noise while still being a real statistical claim, not a tautology.
